summary: Prefetch/health-probe interleaving causes widened pin latency distribution and temporary routing fallback
description: Issue summary: Customer reports spikes in tail latency and intermittent fallback to a degraded variant while a tenant was pinned to a promoted model during a canary window. Impact: A subset of requests for NimbusDocs (~0.6% of traffic) observe token-level latency spikes from ~40ms median to 400-700ms 99th, and ~1 in 2000 requests were routed to the fallback variant for ~2 minutes. Environment: Dedicated pool (d-5g), prod us-west-2, pinned model redwood/open-instruct-v1 pinned by tenant override. Steps to reproduce: 1) Pin tenant to promoted model variant. 2) Trigger prewarm / prefetch on the variant from console (simulate prewarm load). 3) Run an artificial traffic spike with 95/5 short/long sequences. 4) Observe health-probe preflight and edge-side prefetch requests interleaving with live tenant requests. Observed behavior: Health-probe and prefetch jobs intermittently hold edge-connection slots and inject KV-warmup traffic that extends per-request scheduling latency; this causes the routing layer to mark a small number of backend workers as slow and trigger fallback routing for tenant sessions still under pin. Expected behavior: Prewarm/prefetch probes should not affect live pinned sessions' latency or provoke fallback routing. Temporary workaround: Pause prewarm jobs for the tenant and increase canary health thresholds to tolerate brief probe-induced latency increases.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a dedicated tenant in us-west-2 and pin it to redwood/open-instruct-v1 via the Console pin API
Configure prewarm jobs to run with aggressive concurrency (prefetch concurrency = 16) against the same variant
Send mixed short/long request traffic at ~120 rps from the edge for ~5 minutes
Observe edge and orchestrator logs for interleaved probe/prefetch entries and routing decisions
observed_logs: edge-proxy [2026-03-09T21:04:12Z] INFO request_id=abc123 route=tenant-42 backend=worker-7 latency=512ms probe=true
routing-mesh [2026-03-09T21:04:15Z] INFO tenant=tenant-42 decision=fallback target=degraded-variant reason=slow_backend
comments: 2026-03-10 - Sophie Patel: Customer (NimbusDocs) reported spike in tail latency coinciding with an aggressive prewarm run initiated from their CI. They've pinned to a promoted variant for a feature rollout.

2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz: Assigned for triage. Initial hypothesis: prefetch / health probes are counted against the same connection and scheduling quotas used by pinned tenant traffic causing transient slow backend flags.
2026-03-11 - Priya Desai (SRE): Reproduced locally with synthetic prewarm; saw probe traffic occupying worker slots and increasing rendezvous scheduling latency. Attached traces to PR #4521.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz: Confirmed that sticky session tokens remained bound but routing layer evicted a fraction of requests due to short-lived slow_backend marks. Working on a mitigation: isolate prewarm traffic as low-priority and exempt from slow_backend probes while a tenant-level pin is active.
2026-03-12 - Customer (NimbusDocs) via CS: Applied temporary pause of prewarm jobs and saw immediate reduction in fallbacks. Asking for permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Probe: orchestration health checks and console-initiated prewarm jobs share the same worker scheduling window and contribute to connection saturation.
Worker telemetry shows KV cache warming tasks increase first-token completion time which the health-check smoothing algorithm interprets as degraded worker health.
Routing policy currently treats worker marked slow for >300ms as candidate for fallback; short bursts from prewarm can exceed this threshold and trigger reroute.
Repro repo: tests added in serving-runtime perf harness replicating 99th percentile spike when prewarm concurrency > 8 and tenant pinned sessions concurrently active.
Edge behavior: edge-proxy does not annotate prewarm requests in a way that downstream can treat them as non-customer-affinitive leading to incorrect affinity accounting.
proposed_next_steps: Short-term: Add a flag to prewarm/health-probe requests (edge header X-Prewarm: true) to deprioritize scheduling and exclude from slow_backend health metrics (hotfix).
Short-term: Update canary health thresholds for pinned tenants to use conservative smoothing during active pin windows.
Medium-term: Refactor scheduler to isolate prewarm jobs into separate soft-pool with bounded concurrency per node.
Long-term: Add pin-aware QoS where pinned tenant streams have preemptive scheduling priority and probe traffic is shunted to background lanes.
Run a controlled canary of the hotfix in us-west-2 with NimbusDocs before broad rollout.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Hotfix deployed to edge-proxy and orchestrator: prewarm requests now carry X-Prewarm header and are deprioritized by scheduler (PRs 219, 4521).
2026-03-12 - Observed results: fallback rate for NimbusDocs dropped to baseline within 10 minutes of hotfix, 99th latency returned to <120ms for pinned traffic.
Follow-up: Medium-term work item created in backlog (INT-10077) to implement dedicated prewarm soft-pools and pin-aware QoS. Customer will be notified and offered a review call.
Workaround documented: If customers plan large prewarm runs during active pins, schedule prewarm off-window or reduce concurrency until soft-pools are implemented.
final_verdict: Mitigated with hotfix; root cause is scheduling interference from prewarm/health probes. Medium-term scheduler isolation is recommended to prevent recurrence.
resolution_status: Partial fix deployed; monitoring in place. Medium-term follow-up scheduled.
